machine.gpu: none: the WebGPU adapter here is a software one

scope: Twenty-nine effects (one of them a .cube colour table, imported through the upload route and through the editor), the colour looks and thirty-three transitions on synthetic still images at 360x640, on a software WebGPU adapter. Correctness of the passes and of the refusals only: no speed claim, no real footage, no hardware adapter, nobody looked at the pictures.

checks.name: Fixture as imported: green background, red square in the middle
key.chroma (still): the green background is gone (the black project background shows) and the red square is untouched
The same still rendered twice is identical
key.chroma follows its parameters: keying red instead removes the square and keeps the green
key.chroma (editor preview): same result on the preview canvas
Preview and still agree (mean difference under 0.5 of 255)
key.chroma (export): the exported frame shows the same (within video compression)
distort.wave: before the effect the stripe is straight
distort.wave: each row of the stripe is displaced by the sine the parameters describe (within 1 pixel)
distort.wave travels by itself: 0.5 s later the stripe is where a quarter-wave shift puts it (within 1 pixel), and that frame alone gives the same picture again
distort.wave with speed 0 stays still
distort.wave: preview and still agree (mean difference under 0.5 of 255)
No uncaught errors in the editor page
Ramp fixture reads back as itself (the measuring stick: within 1.5 pixels)
distort.bulge: every sampled pixel comes from where the formula says (within 2.5 pixels), and differs from the plain picture
distort.swirl: matches its formula (within 2.5 pixels)
distort.mirror: the right half shows the left half mirrored (within 1.5 pixels)
blur.zoom: each pixel is the average along its streak toward the centre (within 2.5 pixels on a linear ramp)
stylize.posterize with 4 levels leaves only four values per channel
digital.glitch: each band jumps sideways by exactly what the integer hash gives (within 1.5 pixels), some bands jump and some do not, rows never move up or down
digital.glitch: the same frame is identical when rendered again; half a second later the pattern is another one
distort.fisheye: matches its formula (within 2.5 pixels)
distort.kaleidoscope: every wedge shows the first half-wedge, mirrored (within 2.5 pixels away from the folds)
color.grade, saturation 0: every pixel is the grey of its own brightness (within 2 of 255)
color.grade: one stop of exposure doubles the values; a warmer temperature raises red by a tenth and lowers blue by a tenth
Colour looks: 40 are listed; applying one sets the clip's colour grade (noir is black and white), applying another replaces it instead of stacking, an unknown look is refused
stylize.halftone: white paper shows between the dots, the dark corner is darker than the bright corner, and the same frame is identical again
stylize.vhs: at amount 0 the picture is unchanged; at 0.6 it changes, the same frame is identical again, and another frame has another pattern
blur.directional: sideways, pixels near the stripe take the share of the 17 samples that fall on it; along the stripe, nothing changes
blur.tilt-shift: the band stays sharp, far rows are blurred
light.glow: light spills next to the bright stripe, not far from it, and the stripe itself stays
stylize.duotone: black becomes the dark colour and white the light colour
stylize.scanlines: every other line of the 64 is darkened by the amount
light.sparkle: a streak reaches sideways from the bright stripe, fading with distance, and nothing appears far away
motion.shake, pulse, sway and spin: the still at 7/30 s matches the transform the same code computes (within 3 pixels), is identical when rendered again, and differs at another moment
motion.pulse is largest exactly on the beat (every half second at 120 beats per minute) and has settled before the next one

motion.pulse set to follow the music: on a clip under a drum loop whose beats were detected by the analysis, the stills at the frame soonest after a beat and at the frame latest in a beat match the pulse computed from the detected beats (within 3 pixels); the picture is larger near the beat
with the music track muted the same effect falls back to its own tempo setting
light.leak: nothing at amount 0; otherwise it only ever adds light, and the light has moved two seconds later
light.strobe: brightest at the start of each cycle and nearly gone before the next; a rate above three flashes per second is refused

Strobes together, on an exported file: two strobes on a picture and a strobing title over it start at most three flashes in any one second (30 frames), and do keep flashing (at least 2.4 starts a second on average)

Strobes together, in the editor shuttled at 8x: the preview keeps flashing but shows at most three flashes in any second of real time (sampled on every animation frame); the player's safety guard held flashes back, so without it there would have been more
stylize.film: changes the picture, is identical for the same frame, and differs on another frame
digital.rgb-shake: red is taken from exactly the seeded offset (within 1.5 pixels), green stays where it is, another step has another offset, and a frame is identical when rendered again
All 33 GPU transitions start mostly on the outgoing picture, end mostly on the incoming one and never go backwards in between (the flash is checked at its ends only)
Every GPU transition gives the identical middle frame when rendered again, and no two of them give the same middle frame
Soft wipe right, half-way: the left side already shows the incoming picture and the right side still the outgoing one; wipe left is the opposite
Iris open, half-way: the centre shows the incoming picture and the corners the outgoing one; iris close is the opposite
Clock wipe, half-way: the right half is the incoming picture and the left half the outgoing one; reversed is the opposite
Squeeze, half-way: each picture is squeezed into its half, with columns taken from twice as far (within 3 pixels)
Blinds, half-way: in each of the nine slats the first half shows the incoming picture and the second half the outgoing one
A GPU transition in an export: the half-way frame of the file shows the iris as the still does
stylize.edges: the border of the square is bright and the flat areas are dark
Editor with an adapter: the GPU effects are offered and no warning is shown
A .cube file uploaded through the asset route becomes a library entry of kind lut with its size; a junk file and a 1D table named .cube are refused with a typed error and add nothing
color.lut with no table chosen: the still is delivered and is exactly the plain picture
color.lut, intensity 1: every grid pixel of the still is what core sampleStrip gives for the plain still's pixel (within 3 of 255), and the picture did change
color.lut: the same still rendered again is identical
color.lut, intensity 0.5: every grid pixel lies half-way between the plain picture and the table (within 3 of 255); apply_lut replaced the effect instead of stacking a second one
color.lut, intensity 0: the plain picture (largest difference 1 of 255)
Removing the table while the effect uses it is refused, so is placing a table on the timeline, and so is naming a table that does not exist (the refusal lists the tables there are)

A table that cannot be read is not rendered around: the still is refused and the reason names the colour table, not a missing graphics adapter; a table whose bytes are gone blocks the render up front; with the bytes back the still is as before

checks.name: Editor while the table cannot be read: the preview shows the plain picture and a notice over it names the effect and the colour table, not a missing graphics adapter

detail.notice: התמונה מוצגת כרגע בלי האפקט הזה, כי החומר שלו לא נטען. המערכת מנסה שוב מעצמה; ייצוא ותמונות בודדות יסורבו עד שייטען.טבלת צבע (LUT) — colour table ast_c3d873ee630 could not be loaded: Missing LUT_3D_SIZE

checks.name: Editor after the table's bytes are back: without any action the paused preview becomes the graded picture and the notice goes away
color.lut: the editor preview and the still agree (mean difference under 0.5 of 255)

Editor: the effect shows a chooser with "none" and the project's table, selected; intensity keeps its slider; the library card of the table shows its size, is marked as in use, cannot be removed, and has no add-to-timeline or view button
Editor: "import .cube" on the effect uploads the file into the library and selects it for that effect; an identity table changes nothing beyond 2 of 255
Once no effect refers to it, the first table can be removed (and the removal undone)
color.lut with a table declared over the domain 0..2: the still follows the strip model (within 3 of 255) and the file's own definition, core sampleLut (within 4 of 255)

color.lut with input domains that do not line up with the table's grid (0..1.5, and video range 0.0625..0.9375): the still follows the file's own definition, core sampleLut, within 3 of 255 where a finer grid holds every entry and within 4 where none up to 65 does

Fixture with translucent pixels, as imported: over the black background every grid pixel is its colour times its alpha (within 1 of 255); the grid has translucent pixels, pixels with blue = 255 (also translucent ones) and the corner where all three channels are 255

color.lut on translucent pixels and at the top of every channel: every grid pixel is the table's answer for the straight colour, times the pixel's alpha (within 3 of 255), also where blue is 255 (the last slice of the table); a lookup of the premultiplied colour would be far off
color.lut, intensity 0, on translucent pixels: the plain picture (largest difference 1 of 255), so taking the colour out of its premultiplied form and putting it back loses nothing
color.lut (export): the exported frame is the graded picture (within video compression), far from the plain one
No uncaught errors in the editor page with a colour table
Editor without an adapter: the clip is shown WITHOUT the effect (green still there), a warning says why, and the effect cannot be added
